language_wrapper: Consider a cylindrical {rows}×{cols} grid: columns wrap around (so column 1 and column {cols} are adjacent), but rows do not. Color each square either black or white. A black square attacks any square that shares a side or a corner with it, with wrap-around considered horizontally. Determine the number of colorings with exactly {k_black} black squares in which no two black squares attack each other. Give the exact integer.
hardness_rationale: This family counts independent sets on a grid under king-move adjacency with cylindrical wrap-around horizontally and an exact cardinality constraint. The seed only enforces orthogonal adjacency on a planar n×n board and asks for a small sum of totals; here, wrap-around and diagonal constraints create a more complex compatibility graph between rows, and fixing the exact number of black squares introduces an extra DP dimension. A transfer-matrix approach with counting by weight is required; naive guessing or simple recurrence is impractical.
notes: The solver must construct the state space of valid cylindrical row masks and a compatibility graph that enforces vertical and diagonal non-attacking constraints with wrap-around. The DP accumulates exact black counts across rows. Sizes are chosen to keep computation feasible while still requiring careful implementation.
source_question: The number of ways to color an \(n \times n\) chessboard with black and white such that no neighboring two blocks can be black simultaneously is \(x_n\). Find \(\sum_{n=2}^5 x_n\)．
